title: The forty
tomorrow: Dadi's surgery is tomorrow. why is she up at 3 a.m. with her beads?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the ways: the schools, reading the same sources, facing one qibla. Many ways, one. Today closes the week, with the sayings people carry in their pockets.

Every interview, every application, every first date gets around to the same question: so, why are you here? At a weekend-school recital, a seven-year-old steps up to the microphone, grips it with both hands, and opens with a saying of the Prophet ﷺ that asks exactly that. Actions are only by intentions, he says, and each person gets what they intended. Then he forgets the rest and grins, and the room claps anyway.
screen: `SO, WHY ARE YOU HERE?` → `A BOY AT THE MICROPHONE.` → `ACTIONS ARE BY INTENTIONS.`

segments.voice: That saying opens a small book by the scholar al-Nawawi, known simply as the Forty: short, foundational hadith, gathered so a learner could carry the heart of the faith in one pocket. It's in Bukhari and Muslim too. One to tell a friend tonight: it's the very first hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, standing at the door of the whole collection. The word underneath it is niyyah, intention: the why behind the what. The same action, prayer or giving, becomes what you meant it to be. Now hold this week up against that first hadith, and hear its six lines again. The practices hold. By heart. The whole book. Good company. The long line. Many ways, one. Each of them is an action. And each one turns on the same quiet question the boy asked into a microphone: why are you doing this?
screen: `AL-NAWAWI'S FORTY.` · `THE FIRST HADITH IN BUKHARI.` · `NIYYAH: THE WHY BEHIND THE WHAT.` · `SIX LINES, ONE QUESTION.` · then, large: `FORTY FOUNDATIONS.`

segments.voice: Say the first hadith out loud, in your own words: actions are by intentions, and each person gets what they intended. Then choose one thing you'll do in the next hour, even washing a cup, and say quietly why you're doing it. Sit with that why until the time is up.
screen: `SAY THE FIRST HADITH.` · `ONE THING IN THE NEXT HOUR.` · `SAY WHY.`

segments.voice: The forty: al-Nawawi's small book of foundational hadith, opening with intention. A week's lines, carried in one pocket.
Your line for the week's end: forty foundations, and the first one is why. Nine of fifteen, a week done.

howItsDone: Many Muslims study al-Nawawi's Forty Hadith, often memorizing them in weekend schools or study circles, beginning with the hadith that actions are judged by intentions.

fork.setup: you're volunteering at a food drive and catch yourself hoping someone posts a photo of you. what does the first hadith say?
options: the work is wasted now; better to stop than serve with mixed motives.
notice it and set your intention again; each person gets what they intended.
it doesn't matter at all, since the food arrives either way.
fork.reveal: the hadith puts the weight on the why. a mixed motive is a reason to set the intention again, not to quit the good deed.

chat.says: zayd nailed 'actions are by intentions'! then asked: if i help mom just to get candy, does it count?
options: It counts as what he meant it for. He gets what he intended, so aim higher.
Only the helping counts. Why you do something never really matters.
It's worthless now, so he might as well stop helping altogether.
chat.meaning: Actions are by intentions, and each person gets what they intended (Bukhari 1). The why shapes the deed; you can always set it again.
